claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering technical problems including Nvidia driver issues and memory leaks.

citations.review_text: Trash game, has Nvidia drivers issues

Too many particle effects and camera cut slow motion shots that disturb the flow of the game. Too much brainrot, basically. Tekken 7 was SO much better than this. They made every male character a bodybuilder for some reason?? My boy Hwoarang looks so bad and generic. Really disappointed.

Plus there is a memory leak issue and the game runs pathetically bad compared to how average it looks. Granted I have a low end PC but still, Tekken 7 and MK11 looked pretty nice and ran really well. Unreal engine games run so pathetic.

Plus there is a memory leak issue and the game runs pathetically bad compared to how average it looks. Granted I have a low end PC but still, Tekken 7 and MK11 looked pretty nice and ran really well. Unreal engine games run so pathetic.

Over half of my playtime as of writing this review was spent trying to get this game to launch. When it finally did, I was furious. My rig clearly meets the minimum requirements to hit 60 fps, but I can't even break 40 consistently during a fight, or even 30 depending on the stage. Yet as CLEARLY stated in the System Requirements section:

"*"FPS (frame rate/second): Stable over 60" is guaranteed and selected under the graphic settings by default when the game is launched for the first time.*"

100+ gigabytes on what? A story mode people will look up on youtube, graphics only a cutting edge PC can render, and loading in 8k textures? plus locking 4 (FOUR) members of the cast behind paid DLC that costs 75% of the game's total cost... that's just wrong. I bought this through a steam key reseller for half the listed price, and it still wasn't worth that much.

Namco, go back to making Pac-Man, because there's no way you can screw that up any worse than you did with the ghostly adventures.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features an arcade mode that provides tips on combos for preferred fighters.

citations.review_text: It’s a good fighting game. I’d it beginner friendly? Not really but you can adapt with the modes it gives you especially that arcade mode, it gives you some good tips on combos with your preferred fighter. Only problem is the input feels delayed a bit and rank can be a little annoying but overall it’s a good ass fighting game I give it a  8/10 oh and the community is nice, people are willing to spar with you and give you pointers after kicking your ass

As a Tekken instalment it's fun enough, the arcade campaign is nice and I liked the visual style. it's great having all the music and checking out old favorites in the story with the nonsensical canon.

The game systems themselves just don't feel good though, and only got worse after the initial season. It just feels like a weak entry when your actually playing matches. Still enjoyable but wait for sales.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Combat flow faces interruptions from lengthy animations while extra content remains heavily priced.

claims.claim: Mid-match cutscenes, rage arts, and long combos interrupt the flow of combat.

citations.review_text:
Wish i could give this game a like.

I don't have the largest playtime, But its enough for me to say its not enjoyable anymore. It seems like it'd be good to get into but gets worse and worse, they introduced some new mechanics that are dandy the first few hours in but then it gets stale very quickly after seeing them constantly. The mid-match cutscenes burn the flow of combat and kill the vibe. The game suffers from over-aggression in fights and despite the idea of quick matches being ideal to get you pumped up. This does NOT deliver. Make a mistake and your roped into a combo that pretty much ends the fight/prolongs it to an unsavory amount of time. Its just not exciting.

Couple that with the online play, (which understandably is toxic like many games) you don't get room to grow, Ranked matches can only be played to sets of three, meaning you can't just enjoy having fun with your foe for some ungodly reason, many of the players ragequit with no time penalty to halt them from messing with other honest player, Its a disaster. Like if the only fans left are immature children.

I guess to top this off... I can say i was mostly here for online competitive play, but its not worth it, Its just an echo of what it used to be after a while of gameplay. I come back every now and then but find myself quitting after two matches because i recall why i left in the first place. I'm upset to see how much worse it got with each update, its clear monetization was the main goal of this game. More effort is put into making costumes and cosmetics than actually balancing the game and making it worthwhile.

The most garbage Tekken game I ever played. It's full of slow annoying cut scenes that constantly fill the screen with blue every single round. You spend half the match watching blue cut scenes, rage arts, and 20 second long combos. It's 30% gameplay, and 70% watching a cut scene or combo. Horrendous fighting game that needs to go back to the drawing board. At this rate Tekken 9 will probably be a QTE fighter. Older Tekken games used to be SO FAST PACED with zero cut scenes. They really ruined Tekken 8 with this horrendously slow and vomit inducing "gameplay".

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features high-priced downloadable content.

citations.review_text:
Easily the most aggressive, fast paced Tekken yet. I am no master, I play a few fighting games but I never connect with them, like I connect with Tekken. If you're a fan of the series, this is just an absolute blast. 

The story is as insane as always, your mileage may vary in regards to how many silly haircuts you can see in one cutscene. It was enjoyable though and the last fight was a cinematic explosion of over the top action. 

The roster is huge, varied and like all Tekken games, deep as an ocean. There are good options for online and offline play, as well as ghosts of players you have played and some of the best tutorial/training systems going. You can watch a replay of your last match and it will tell you where you messed up and how you might be able to counter it. 

The DLC is very expensive, I understand making and balancing characters is difficult and that is fairly reflected. The cost of the extra maps and cosmetics is a bit rich for me.

Nonetheless, this is an amazing game, I hope to see you out there, at the end of my fist.

I like the game but the main negative points 

*prices are too high for every DLC and if you have to pay for full package
in gameplay 
*Staying in the air for 10 to 15 seconds every round is too boring -.- make it 4 or 5 hits for 50% better than 15 hits for 50%  reduce the air time

claims.claim: Reviewers note that online matches suffer from unexpected disconnections on Steam that mimic manual player plug-outs.

citations.review_text:
Season 3 patch is great but still has some issues

As of season 3 Tekken feels balanced as they the nerfed heat mechanic and every characters heat smash and a lot of nerfs across the board. Some characters will feel too oppressive, but that could be skill issue or just need some labbing to get matchup knowledge.

My issue is that on a few occassions Steam will disconnect me from an ongoing online match, making me look like I plugged out. Tekken is the only game that does this to me.

So this will be biased in some way but also this is me completely chewing them out as a fan...
I love tekken and have played it since i was a little girl,
but like the crashes on startup is ridiculous and its been a problem for months now on higher end PC's...
I honestly would love to talk about and tell people about how engaging and challenging the game is especially online,but i cant even do that because for the past 2 months maybe more im getting nothing but a video allocation error and a fatal error? 
Much time spent in this game but please...if consoles can handle this game better...whats the point?

claims.claim: Reviewers state that DLC characters are locked and cannot be practiced against without purchasing them.

citations.review_text:
Multiplayer is disapointing because of the negatives aspects of the game. The positive ones do not compensate those in my oppinion. Therefore it is not worth paying your money for this game.

Very bad matchmacking which is the main reason of taking away the joy of playing multiplayer (being matched 9 of 10 times vs other ranks instead of the same rank), 
Payed DLC which you cannot disable or practice against without paying. Players using these have an advantage.
Lame playstyle pays off, players can use a keyboard or leverless pads to have an advantage over players using a controller. Especially for the fast movement this works in their advantage.

If the matchmaking was not so bad many of these negative points would be compensated and wouldn't matter but this is not the case.

Would not recommend to buy unless you play offline only or only against friends. Got many hours in this game just with friends and for that it can be enjoyable.

"PLUS ON BLOCK"

Even with "modern tekken" characters, the game is still fundamentally the same as I remember from 3 and 5, it's just a lot flashier, (a hell of a lot greedier with their pricing, character customization and locking DLC characters from training), a lot heaver on GPUs thanks to UE5, and a hell of a lot faster. This is one of the most aggressive fighters on the market - pick this one if you like spamming buttons and aren't too concerned about frame data and getting frame-perfect special inputs or "links." They exist, but you don't always need them.

I dislike 6 button fighters, this 4 button fighter feels intuitive. There are actually very few combo strings - Most attacks flow into other stances or other attacks, and you can generally find out what these stances do pretty quickly and string together your own mixups and combos fluidly without needing to spend time learning strict frame data. There's over 100 attacks based on stances - standing up, back turned, while side stepping, from the ground, in various stances, pressing two buttons together... It sounds intimidating but it flows pretty well, and keeps every fight fresh - every fight you'll discover new things about your character and your opponent. 

While it's slid much further away from its classic martial arts style into a more stylish anything goes weapons and guns are OK type fighter (excluding Yoshimitsu), it's such a fun aggressive fighter that still has the core of what made tekken great. There are so many options you have that new players are able to execute combos and expert players are able to counter with heavy mixup hits.

Heat sucks. Then you get better, and you like it. Then it sucks. Then it rocks again.

The best to Harada's new ventures

claims.claim: Reviewers report that defensive mechanics such as sidesteps, backdashes, and blocking have been made obsolete or worse, while gameplay heavily rewards aggressive button mashing and rushdown tactics.

citations.review_text:
I've been playing tekken since Tekken Tag 1 of the PS2 days, and I've had nothing but fond memories leading up to now. Ever since the season 2 patch, it's been nothing but downhill.

Characters are all homogenized where almost everyone is rushdown. Combos are way longer than it really needs to be, EVERYONE has some sort of string into a stance which leads to another string then stance, etc. Characters transition from previous tekken games to tekken 8 go through some drastic change, which made me drop several of my roster (ex. Steve, Anna, Devil Jin, Jin, Lee, etc.). And there's hardly ANY neutral in the game, it's just rushdown rushdown rushdown.

I really want to love Tekken 8, I really do. But with so many changes made to the game, I'm ready for Tekken to either come up with a new game and start from scratch, or just wait for the end of Tekken.

Tekken 8 started out incredibly strong, and with a pretty strong campaign (50% fan services executed wonderfully well) and strong new systems movesets. There was promise. 

After season 2 though, the game's mechanics have all learned so hard into aggression that there's not really any tactics left. Sidesteps, Backdashes, Blocking. Essentially all defensive tech was made either worse or downright obsolete. Worse of all, the updated movesets, which could've been a way to increase player expression have devolved into giving each character 50/50 moves that makes things less about strategy and more random. 

The singleplayer campaign got one expansion that actively made Tekken 7's ending less meaningful. No new game modes, not even something as simple as survival and gold battles, mainstays of previous entries. 

It's Tekken at its flashiest, but at its least intentional. If, like me, you played for engaging battles that required thinking and strategies, that's long gone.

This game has been hyped from the very start of the game. It has been enjoyable but once you start getting to the point of understanding the frustration and the button mashing of the game which is the sole purpose of this game, then it's just burn out from the game and no longer wanting to play the game at all. 

I Know i got 137 hours in the game, but tekken 7 i have 100 hours more added to that game and there's a reason why i love Tekken 7 than this tekken 8 trash. The reason is Tekken 7 have more defensive mechanics, more rewarding gameplay and the low parries are something that is spectacular. In Tekken 8, it's all just mashing the buttons and play the aggressor and you win the game in which you might enjoy for a few months then it all starts crashing down from the view point of mechanics being trash and condescending.

I Will leave my review like this for now. Until then i don't want to play this game anymore as this has burnt me out in just 4 months of playing the game.

The developers of this game seem to want to cater to a certain demographic. Not the players that focus on improving fundamentals (Sidestepping, Whiff punishment, Blocking). Instead they would rather cater to players that want to turn their brains off and just mash their way to victory. They do not want their precious coco melon casuals to feel bad when being punished for a mistake, rather, they want to make them feel good, so they make every move safe on block, every move have insane tracking, and when a move isn't safe on block, they rely on power crush to cover for their mistakes AND THEN THAT is safe on block. And of course, they make ranking up easier to satisfy the casuals into believing they are improving, when in reality, they just get punished less. JUST LIKE HOW THEY PLAY. They need to nerf all these obnoxious strings that auto track, nerf the power crushes to were they ALL are launch punishable and then MAYBE, this game will feel rewarding to players who actually put the time into learning, not the players who rely on gimmicks and having their hands held.

Tekken 8 has taken a turn for the worst encouraging braindead aggression and encouraging skilless defense/comeback mechanics like rage arts and safe high power crushes. I miss the good days of tekken from tekken 5 to tekken 7. Unfortunately, the game keeps getting dumbed down with each iteration. I feel like Tekken is starting to lose its skill expression. Been playing for years and reached God of Destruction with Steve.
